ci.run:
command -v gh >/dev/null || { echo "gh not found: no CI to wait for"; exit 0; }
pr=$(gh pr view --json number -q .number) || exit 1
sha=$(gh pr view --json headRefOid -q .headRefOid) || exit 1
n=0

  n=$(gh pr view "$pr" --json statusCheckRollup -q '.statusCheckRollup | length') || exit 1

gh pr checks "$pr"
for run in $(gh run list --commit "$sha" --status failure --json databaseId -q '.[].databaseId'); do
  gh run view "$run" --log-failed | tail -200
done
exit 1

quick.source:
# Quick workflow — example installed by `norn init`; edit freely (W1).
# For refactors, docs, chores, other small changes and the fix of a bug a reproduce round confirmed.
# A story workflow without `slices` (W8): every step works in the story worktree. Bring the story up
# to date with its base, implement, bring it up to date again, check, review, describe, open the
# draft PR (or rewrite the body of the open one), wait for the PR's CI, and wait for a person at
# ready; the person merges the PR.
# A story waiting at ready goes back through update when the base moved under it in a way
# that conflicts (BS6–BS8, base.stale: conflict).
# Change `test.run` to your repo's test command.
name: quick
description: Make a small change (refactor, docs, chore, a reproduced bug's fix), check and review it, open the draft PR, wait for CI.
start: sync
steps:
  # brings the story branch up to date with its base before any code is written, so implement starts
  # from the current base and the update after it merges only what moved meanwhile
  sync:
    type: git
    action: update
    outcomes: { done: implement, conflict: { to: sync-resolve, counter: sync_conflict_loop } }
  sync-resolve:
    type: agent
    skill: norn-merge
    inputs: [spec, handoff]
    instructions: "Base mode: merge the base commit named in Rework into the story branch in this worktree, resolve, commit the merge; never rebase."
    outcomes:
      done: { to: sync, means: "base merged into the story branch, conflicts resolved and committed" }
  implement:
    type: agent
    skill: norn-implement
    inputs: [spec, handoff, last_check, last_findings]
    instructions: >-
      Work from what the story already holds: the Plan section of spec.md when a refinement round wrote one,
      otherwise the issue mirrored in spec.md and its latest `## Triage` comment. Keep to what they ask.
      A change in behaviour gets a test first; a change to docs or a pure refactor needs none beyond the
      suite staying green. A bug comes from a reproduce round with a red loop in the handoff's Progress and
      the issue's latest `## Reproduce` comment: turn it into a failing test at the seam named there before
      changing any code, then fix the cause.
    outcomes:
      done: { to: update, means: "the change is made; each behaviour change and rework point has a passing test" }
  update:
    type: git
    action: update
    outcomes: { done: test, conflict: { to: resolve, counter: base_conflict_loop } }
  resolve:
    type: agent
    skill: norn-merge
    inputs: [spec, handoff]
    instructions: "Base mode: merge the base commit named in Rework into the story branch in this worktree, resolve, commit the merge; never rebase."
    outcomes:
      done: { to: update, means: "base merged into the story branch, conflicts resolved and committed" }
  test:
    type: check
    run: bun test
    timeout: 15m
    outcomes: { pass: review, fail: { to: implement, counter: test_loop } }
  review:
    type: agent
    skill: norn-review
    inputs: [spec, diff]
    outcomes:
      approve:           { to: describe, means: "the change does what the story asks and nothing else, no blocking findings" }
      changes_requested: { to: implement, counter: review_loop, means: "blocking findings in the receipt" }
  describe:
    type: agent
    skill: norn-pr
    inputs: [spec, diff, handoff]
    instructions: "Write the PR body to pr.md in the spec folder; norn puts the issue link under it."
    outcomes:
      done: { to: open-pr, means: "pr.md describes the branch as it is now: summary, evidence, merge danger" }
  open-pr:
    type: git
    action: open-pr
    outcomes: { done: ci }
  # waits for the checks on the PR's head commit (a detached check run, so the tick is not blocked):
  # up to 5m for a first check to appear, none means the repo has no CI and passes; a red check's
  # failed log becomes last_check for implement, whose rework goes back through open-pr to the new head.
  # GitHub (gh) only: on GitLab replace the script, or route open-pr's done straight to ready.
  ci:
    type: check
    run: |
      command -v gh >/dev/null || { echo "gh not found: no CI to wait for"; exit 0; }
      pr=$(gh pr view --json number -q .number) || exit 1
      sha=$(gh pr view --json headRefOid -q .headRefOid) || exit 1
      n=0
      for i in $(seq 1 30); do
        n=$(gh pr view "$pr" --json statusCheckRollup -q '.statusCheckRollup | length') || exit 1
        [ "$n" -gt 0 ] && break
        sleep 10
      done
      [ "$n" -gt 0 ] || { echo "no checks on PR #$pr after 5m: nothing to wait for"; exit 0; }
      gh pr checks "$pr" --watch --interval 30 >/dev/null && exit 0
      gh pr checks "$pr"
      for run in $(gh run list --commit "$sha" --status failure --json databaseId -q '.[].databaseId'); do
        gh run view "$run" --log-failed | tail -200
      done
      exit 1
    timeout: 30m
    outcomes: { pass: ready, fail: { to: implement, counter: ci_loop } }
  ready:
    type: gate
    prompt: "Read the draft PR. Approve to mark the story finished (a person still merges the PR), or reject with what to change."
    outcomes:
      approve: $done
      reject:  { to: implement, counter: ready_loop }
      stale:   { to: update, counter: stale_loop }
counters:
  test_loop: { max: 5 }
  ci_loop: { max: 3 }
  review_loop: { max: 3 }
  ready_loop: { max: 2 }
  # reset each time their update merges cleanly: only repeated conflicts on one base move count (W4)
  sync_conflict_loop: { max: 2, reset_on: sync.done }
  base_conflict_loop: { max: 2, reset_on: update.done }
  # a stale re-entry is progress from outside (a sibling merged), bounded by the sibling merges
  stale_loop: { max: 10 }
# update-branch re-enters update, not sync (the default would be the first update step, BS9)
base: { stale: conflict, step: update }

refinement.name: refinement

workflow.name: refinement
workflow.description: Agree a story's spec and plan with a person, against the current base; no code.

sync-resolve.instructions: Base mode: merge the base commit named in Rework into the story branch in this worktree, resolve, commit the merge; never rebase.

done.means: base merged into the story branch, conflicts resolved and committed

refine.instructions: Write the spec into the body of spec.md; keep its frontmatter unchanged.

done.means: spec complete: problem, solution, numbered Behaviour items with examples, out of scope; no open questions

questions.means: spec written, but open questions are listed that need the person's answers

done.means: every open question is answered and folded into the spec

plan.instructions: Write the Plan section of spec.md.

done.means: spec.md's Plan section has seams, a coverage table for every Behaviour item, prefactoring, decisions and risks

refinement.source:
# Refinement workflow — example installed by `norn init`; edit freely (W1).
# Brings the story up to date with its base, so the spec and plan are written against the current
# code, then refines the spec, settles its open questions and plans it, all with a person (attended).
# It cuts no slices and has no gate: starting the next round (`norn story edit <story> --workflow story`
# or `--workflow quick`) is the person's approval of the plan. To rework the plan, start a new
# refinement round at plan (`--workflow refinement --at plan`).
name: refinement
description: Agree a story's spec and plan with a person, against the current base; no code.
start: sync
steps:
  sync:
    type: git
    action: update
    outcomes: { done: refine, conflict: { to: sync-resolve, counter: sync_conflict_loop } }
  sync-resolve:
    type: agent
    skill: norn-merge
    inputs: [spec, handoff]
    instructions: "Base mode: merge the base commit named in Rework into the story branch in this worktree, resolve, commit the merge; never rebase."
    outcomes:
      done: { to: sync, means: "base merged into the story branch, conflicts resolved and committed" }
  refine:
    type: agent
    skill: norn-refine
    attended: true
    inputs: [spec, handoff]
    instructions: "Write the spec into the body of spec.md; keep its frontmatter unchanged."
    outcomes:
      done:      { to: plan, means: "spec complete: problem, solution, numbered Behaviour items with examples, out of scope; no open questions" }
      questions: { to: clarify, means: "spec written, but open questions are listed that need the person's answers" }
  clarify:
    type: agent
    skill: norn-clarify
    attended: true
    inputs: [spec, handoff]
    outcomes:
      done: { to: plan, means: "every open question is answered and folded into the spec" }
  plan:
    type: agent
    skill: norn-plan
    attended: true
    inputs: [spec, handoff]
    instructions: "Write the Plan section of spec.md."
    outcomes:
      done: { to: $done, means: "spec.md's Plan section has seams, a coverage table for every Behaviour item, prefactoring, decisions and risks" }
counters:
  # resets each time sync merges cleanly: only repeated conflicts on one base move count (W4)
  sync_conflict_loop: { max: 2, reset_on: sync.done }

reproduce.name: reproduce

workflow.name: reproduce
workflow.description: Reproduce a bug through the real interface, confirm its cause and the seam for a regression test; change no code.

reproduce.instructions: The issue is mirrored in spec.md; read its comments too. First follow the report as a user, through the real interface (the UI, the command, the request), and record what you saw. Then build a loop that goes red on that exact symptom, minimise it and confirm the cause. You are told not to fix: change no file, spec.md included, but the handoff. Post the findings as an issue comment that starts with `## Reproduce` (`## Reproduce (updated)` on a rerun): the loop command, the minimised repro, what it prints, the confirmed cause (`file:line`, or the ranked hypotheses left) and the seam for a regression test. That one comment is the only remote write this step allows, an exception to the norn skill's rule; never edit the issue, label, assign or close. Write the same under Progress in the handoff (the next agent does not see your Resume).

reproduced.means: the bug was observed as a user and a loop goes red on it; loop, repro, cause and seam posted and in the handoff

cannot_reproduce.means: followed the report faithfully and the bug did not occur, nor in any loop tried; what was tried posted and in the handoff

reproduce.source:
# Reproduce workflow — example installed by `norn init`; edit freely (W1).
# Select it with the issue label norn:wf:reproduce, or start it after triage
# (`norn story edit <story> --workflow reproduce`).
# An unattended agent follows the report through the real interface, builds a loop that goes red on
# the symptom, minimises it, confirms the cause and names the seam for a regression test. It posts
# all of that as an issue comment and changes no code. Every outcome ends the round ($done): the fix
# is a quick round (`--workflow quick`), whose implement turns the red loop into a failing test first,
# or a refinement round when the fix needs a design.
# Reproduce changes no code and opens no PR, so it has no base sync (BS*).
name: reproduce
description: Reproduce a bug through the real interface, confirm its cause and the seam for a regression test; change no code.
start: reproduce
steps:
  reproduce:
    type: agent
    skill: norn-diagnose
    inputs: [spec, handoff]
    instructions: >-
      The issue is mirrored in spec.md; read its comments too. First follow the report as a user, through
      the real interface (the UI, the command, the request), and record what you saw. Then build a loop
      that goes red on that exact symptom, minimise it and confirm the cause. You are told not to fix:
      change no file, spec.md included, but the handoff.
      Post the findings as an issue comment that starts with `## Reproduce` (`## Reproduce (updated)` on a rerun):
      the loop command, the minimised repro, what it prints, the confirmed cause (`file:line`, or the ranked
      hypotheses left) and the seam for a regression test. That one comment is the only remote write this
      step allows, an exception to the norn skill's rule; never edit the issue, label, assign or close.
      Write the same under Progress in the handoff (the next agent does not see your Resume).
    outcomes:
      reproduced:       { to: $done, means: "the bug was observed as a user and a loop goes red on it; loop, repro, cause and seam posted and in the handoff" }
      cannot_reproduce: { to: $done, means: "followed the report faithfully and the bug did not occur, nor in any loop tried; what was tried posted and in the handoff" }

slice.name: slice

workflow.name: slice
workflow.description: Build one slice test-first, check and review it, and integrate it into the story branch.

done.means: every acceptance criterion (or rework point) has a passing test

approve.means: all criteria met, no blocking findings

done.means: conflicts resolved keeping the intent of both sides; tests pass

slice.source:
# Slice workflow — example installed by `norn init`; edit freely (W1).
# Runs on a slice: build test-first, check, review, then integrate into the story branch.
# A slice has no QA of its own: its criteria stay in its file and the story's qa checks them all, once.
# Change `test.run` to your repo's test command.
name: slice
description: Build one slice test-first, check and review it, and integrate it into the story branch.
start: implement
steps:
  implement:
    type: agent
    skill: norn-implement
    inputs: [slice, spec, handoff, last_check, last_findings]
    outcomes: { done: { to: test, means: "every acceptance criterion (or rework point) has a passing test" } }
  test:
    type: check
    run: bun test
    timeout: 10m
    outcomes: { pass: review, fail: { to: implement, counter: test_loop } }
  review:
    type: agent
    skill: norn-review
    inputs: [slice, spec, diff]
    outcomes:
      approve:           { to: integrate, means: "all criteria met, no blocking findings" }
      changes_requested: { to: implement, counter: review_loop, means: "blocking findings in the receipt" }
  integrate:
    type: git
    action: integrate
    outcomes: { done: $done, conflict: { to: merge, counter: conflict_loop } }
  merge:
    type: agent
    skill: norn-merge
    inputs: [slice, spec]
    outcomes: { done: { to: integrate, means: "conflicts resolved keeping the intent of both sides; tests pass" } }
counters: { test_loop: { max: 5 }, review_loop: { max: 3 }, conflict_loop: { max: 2 } }

story.name: story

workflow.name: story
workflow.description: Slice a planned story against the current base, run the slices, verify the story, open the draft PR, wait for CI.

sync-resolve.instructions: Base mode: merge the base commit named in Rework into the story branch in this worktree, resolve, commit the merge; never rebase.

done.means: base merged into the story branch, conflicts resolved and committed

slice.instructions: Write slice files to slices/<nn>-<slug>.md in the spec folder. A slice has no QA of its own: list every slice's criteria in spec.md's frontmatter `criteria` too, each id prefixed with its slice number (`01.AC1`), next to the story's own, so the story's QA gives each one a verdict. First check the Plan section of spec.md against the code on this base: when spec.md has no Plan section, or the base changed what the plan relies on so that it no longer holds, write no slice files, say what no longer holds in the handoff's Progress and report `replan`.

done.means: slice files written against the current base; every Behaviour item is covered by some slice's acceptance

replan.means: spec.md has no Plan, or the base no longer fits it: what no longer holds is in the handoff; the person replans with `norn story edit <story> --workflow refinement --at plan`

approve-slices.prompt: Review the slice files in the spec folder (edit them if needed). Approve to start the slices, or reject with what to change.

resolve.instructions: Base mode: merge the base commit named in Rework into the story branch in this worktree, resolve, commit the merge; never rebase.

done.means: base merged into the story branch, conflicts resolved and committed

qa.instructions: The criteria are spec.md's frontmatter `criteria`; an id `<nn>.<id>` is criterion `<id>` of slice file `<nn>-*.md`, which says what it means.

pass.means: every acceptance criterion of the story and its slices observed with evidence

fail.means: a criterion fails; repro in findings

partial.means: criteria only a person can judge, evidence prepared

unverified.means: criteria this session could not check; how to check each one is in the report

human-qa.prompt: Check the criteria QA could not settle (listed with how to check each). Approve, or reject with what failed.

done.means: every rework point has a passing test

describe.instructions: Write the PR body to pr.md in the spec folder; norn puts the issue link under it.

done.means: pr.md describes the branch as it is now: summary, evidence, merge danger

story.source:
# Story workflow — example installed by `norn init`; edit freely (W1).
# Delivers a story whose spec and plan a refinement round agreed: bring the story up to date with its
# base, cut slices from the plan against that base, approve them, run the slices, bring the story up
# to date again, verify the whole story once (QA over every slice's criteria), describe it, open the
# draft PR (or rewrite the body of the open one), wait for the PR's CI, and wait for a person at ready.
# Rework found by the story-level test, QA or CI is done in the story worktree.
# QA reports a verdict per acceptance criterion (criteria: required) and may only report the outcome
# matching its worst verdict; `unverified` (could not check here) goes to a person at human-qa.
# A story waiting at human-qa or ready goes back through update when the base moved
# under it in a way that conflicts (base.stale; `behind` re-updates on any base commit).
# Change `test.run` to your repo's test command.
name: story
description: Slice a planned story against the current base, run the slices, verify the story, open the draft PR, wait for CI.
start: sync
steps:
  # brings the story branch up to date with its base before the slices are cut, so they are cut
  # against the code they will change
  sync:
    type: git
    action: update
    outcomes: { done: slice, conflict: { to: sync-resolve, counter: sync_conflict_loop } }
  sync-resolve:
    type: agent
    skill: norn-merge
    inputs: [spec, handoff]
    instructions: "Base mode: merge the base commit named in Rework into the story branch in this worktree, resolve, commit the merge; never rebase."
    outcomes:
      done: { to: sync, means: "base merged into the story branch, conflicts resolved and committed" }
  slice:
    type: agent
    skill: norn-slice
    inputs: [spec, slices]
    instructions: >-
      Write slice files to slices/<nn>-<slug>.md in the spec folder. A slice has no QA of its own: list every
      slice's criteria in spec.md's frontmatter `criteria` too, each id prefixed with its slice number
      (`01.AC1`), next to the story's own, so the story's QA gives each one a verdict. First check the Plan section of spec.md
      against the code on this base: when spec.md has no Plan section, or the base changed what the plan
      relies on so that it no longer holds, write no slice files, say what no longer holds in the handoff's
      Progress and report `replan`.
    outcomes:
      done:   { to: approve-slices, means: "slice files written against the current base; every Behaviour item is covered by some slice's acceptance" }
      replan: { to: $stuck, means: "spec.md has no Plan, or the base no longer fits it: what no longer holds is in the handoff; the person replans with `norn story edit <story> --workflow refinement --at plan`" }
  approve-slices:
    type: gate
    prompt: "Review the slice files in the spec folder (edit them if needed). Approve to start the slices, or reject with what to change."
    outcomes: { approve: slices, reject: { to: slice, counter: slice_loop } }
  slices:
    type: slices
    outcomes: { done: update, stuck: $stuck }
  update:
    type: git
    action: update
    outcomes: { done: test, conflict: { to: resolve, counter: base_conflict_loop } }
  resolve:
    type: agent
    skill: norn-merge
    inputs: [spec, handoff]
    instructions: "Base mode: merge the base commit named in Rework into the story branch in this worktree, resolve, commit the merge; never rebase."
    outcomes:
      done: { to: update, means: "base merged into the story branch, conflicts resolved and committed" }
  test:
    type: check
    run: bun test
    timeout: 15m
    outcomes: { pass: qa, fail: { to: implement, counter: test_loop } }
  qa:
    type: agent
    skill: norn-qa
    inputs: [spec, slices, diff]
    criteria: required
    instructions: "The criteria are spec.md's frontmatter `criteria`; an id `<nn>.<id>` is criterion `<id>` of slice file `<nn>-*.md`, which says what it means."
    outcomes:
      pass:       { to: describe, verdict: pass, means: "every acceptance criterion of the story and its slices observed with evidence" }
      fail:       { to: implement, counter: qa_loop, verdict: fail, means: "a criterion fails; repro in findings" }
      partial:    { to: human-qa, verdict: person, means: "criteria only a person can judge, evidence prepared" }
      unverified: { to: human-qa, verdict: unverified, means: "criteria this session could not check; how to check each one is in the report" }
  human-qa:
    type: gate
    prompt: "Check the criteria QA could not settle (listed with how to check each). Approve, or reject with what failed."
    outcomes:
      approve: describe
      reject:  { to: implement, counter: qa_loop }
      stale:   { to: update, counter: stale_loop }
  implement:
    type: agent
    skill: norn-implement
    inputs: [spec, handoff, last_check, last_findings]
    outcomes:
      done: { to: test, means: "every rework point has a passing test" }
  describe:
    type: agent
    skill: norn-pr
    inputs: [spec, diff, record]
    instructions: "Write the PR body to pr.md in the spec folder; norn puts the issue link under it."
    outcomes:
      done: { to: open-pr, means: "pr.md describes the branch as it is now: summary, evidence, merge danger" }
  open-pr:
    type: git
    action: open-pr
    outcomes: { done: ci }
  # waits for the checks on the PR's head commit (a detached check run, so the tick is not blocked):
  # up to 5m for a first check to appear, none means the repo has no CI and passes; a red check's
  # failed log becomes last_check for implement, whose rework goes back through open-pr to the new head.
  # GitHub (gh) only: on GitLab replace the script, or route open-pr's done straight to ready.
  ci:
    type: check
    run: |
      command -v gh >/dev/null || { echo "gh not found: no CI to wait for"; exit 0; }
      pr=$(gh pr view --json number -q .number) || exit 1
      sha=$(gh pr view --json headRefOid -q .headRefOid) || exit 1
      n=0
      for i in $(seq 1 30); do
        n=$(gh pr view "$pr" --json statusCheckRollup -q '.statusCheckRollup | length') || exit 1
        [ "$n" -gt 0 ] && break
        sleep 10
      done
      [ "$n" -gt 0 ] || { echo "no checks on PR #$pr after 5m: nothing to wait for"; exit 0; }
      gh pr checks "$pr" --watch --interval 30 >/dev/null && exit 0
      gh pr checks "$pr"
      for run in $(gh run list --commit "$sha" --status failure --json databaseId -q '.[].databaseId'); do
        gh run view "$run" --log-failed | tail -200
      done
      exit 1
    timeout: 30m
    outcomes: { pass: ready, fail: { to: implement, counter: ci_loop } }
  ready:
    type: gate
    prompt: "Read the draft PR. Approve to mark the story finished (a person still merges the PR), or reject with what to change."
    outcomes:
      approve: $done
      reject:  { to: implement, counter: ready_loop }
      stale:   { to: update, counter: stale_loop }
counters:
  slice_loop: { max: 3 }
  test_loop: { max: 5 }
  ci_loop: { max: 3 }
  qa_loop: { max: 2 }
  ready_loop: { max: 2 }
  # reset each time their update merges cleanly: only repeated conflicts on one base move count (W4)
  sync_conflict_loop: { max: 2, reset_on: sync.done }
  base_conflict_loop: { max: 2, reset_on: update.done }
  # a stale re-entry is progress from outside (a sibling merged), bounded by the sibling merges
  stale_loop: { max: 10 }
# update-branch re-enters update, not sync (the default would be the first update step, BS9)
base: { stale: conflict, step: update }

triage.source:
# Triage workflow — example installed by `norn init`, the default for a new story
# (config `workflow`); edit freely (W1).
# An unattended agent checks the issue still holds on the base and posts its findings and one
# recommendation as an issue comment, the one place the recommendation lives (the outcome is plain
# `done`). That ends the round ($done): the person reads the comment and starts the next round with
# `norn story edit <story> --workflow refinement|quick|reproduce`, or closes the issue.
# Triage changes no file and opens no PR, so it has no base sync (BS*).
name: triage
description: Check an issue still holds, add its context, and recommend what comes next (refinement, quick, reproduce) or closing it.
start: explore
steps:
  explore:
    type: agent
    skill: norn-triage
    inputs: [spec, handoff]
    instructions: >-
      The issue is mirrored in spec.md. Post the `## Triage` comment on it and add the kind, risk and priority
      labels (GR11): `norn:kind:bug|feature|security|chore|docs`, `norn:risk:low|medium|high`,
      `norn:priority:low|medium|high|extreme`; a label missing on the remote is named in the comment with
      "norn upgrade creates it". That comment and those labels are the only remote writes this step allows,
      an exception to the norn skill's rule; never remove a label, the intake label `norn` included. Change no file, spec.md included,
      but the handoff. The recommendation lives only in that comment:
      report `norn done done --handoff "<recommendation>: <reason>"`.
    outcomes:
      done: { to: $done, means: "the ## Triage comment is posted, with one recommendation (refinement, quick, reproduce or close) and its reason, and the kind, risk and priority labels that could be set are on the issue" }
